EmailTemplate.subject: Thank you for your interest in graduate studies at ASU!
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Dear {!Contact.FirstName},
Thank you for your interest in graduate studies at the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts School of Music at ASU. As one of the largest universities in the country, the ASU School of Music awards over $2 million to students annually, providing an excellent education at an unbeatable value. ASU's diverse and innovative community is a perfect complement to the personal attention you will receive in the School of Music. With a population of around 750 students, we offer small class sizes, state-of-the-art facilities and one-on-one instruction from world-renowned faculty. We invite you to consider the ASU School of Music for this important step in your music studies. Applications for 2017 admission will be available on the School of Music website in August. If you are interested in future study at ASU, please review the information below as guidelines for what to expect when you are ready to apply. For an idea of the course requirements for the various degree programs offered, select one of the checksheets accessible by your degree program interest here. Tuition and fees at Arizona State University are reasonable, even for non-resident students. Music Scholarships and teaching assistantships are available. Typical assistantships are 25% which amount to 10 hours or work per week and receive: · Tuition remission covering the non-resident portion of tuition · 50% reduction in the resident portion of tuition (excluding fees) · $7,450 stipend for the academic year, distributed over bi-weekly paychecks Spoken English requirement: If your native language is not English you must meet spoken English requirements before you can be considered for teaching assistantship. You may complete the ASU SPEAK test (minimum score of 55).Those wishing to be considered for Graduate Teaching Assistantships should submit a TA application by February 15 for an appointment beginning Fall semester. A few reminders for prospective international graduate students: If you are from a country whose native language is not English, you must provide proof of English proficiency. Acceptable proof is as follows: · TOEFL score of at least 550 (PBT) or 80 (iBT) · IELTS overall band score of at least 6.5 with no band below 6.0 · Pearson Test of English (PTE) score of at least 60 It is strongly recommended to complete and pass the English proficiency exam prior to beginning the application process. Scores will be accepted for exams taken up to two years prior to your semester of admission. Applications submitted without a passing TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE score will not be considered for admission. For more information, please visit the Graduate Education English proficiency website. Another good resource for information on the international student application process is here. In addition to University tuition and fees, international students are required to enroll in the ASU student health insurance plan. More information about this requirement can be found here. 3. All transcripts and exam scores must be submitted directly to the Graduate University Admissions office. To process your application, all international records and official academic credentials must be submitted in the original language accompanied by an official English translation. Translations must be literal, complete versions of the originals and must be translated by a university, government official or official translation service. You cannot do your own translation. Application Process Step 1. You must first submit the Graduate Admissions application, followed by the School of Music application, before an audition or interview will be scheduled. Step 2: All transcripts and test scores must be submitted directly to the Graduate Admissions Office of the University. Step 3: Auditions or Interviews will be scheduled and application materials will be reviewed only after all application materials have been submitted. We are not responsible for application materials sent to the wrong office or directly to faculty. Please check the Graduate Education website for application information, and the School of Music website for specific application requirements for your degree program. Applicants to the PhD Music Education, PhD Musicology, and DMA Composition programs must submit GRE scores. The GRE examination in Music is not acceptable for admission to the doctoral program. GRE scores must be from within 5 years prior to the first day of the enrollment term. Due to the high volume of applicants we receive each year, we recommend that you plan to apply as early as possible. Application Deadlines Spring Admission: The application deadline is October 15 for all degrees except for the following programs with prescreening requirements: · All voice concentrations · MM Composition · DMA Composition (Composition, Interdisciplinary Digital Media) · DMA Conducting · DMA Performance The deadline for the above listed programs is October 1. Prescreening Materials are uploaded in the School of Music application and must be received by October 1 for Spring admission and December 1 for Fall admission. For more information visit: https://music.asu.edu/admissions/graduate-auditions. Fall Admission: The application deadline is December 1 for all degrees except for the following programs with rolling deadlines: MM Music Education PhD Music Education MM Music Therapy
Prescreening Materials: these materials uploaded in the School of Music application and must be received by October 1 for Spring admission and December 1 for Fall admission. For more information visit: https://music.asu.edu/admissions/graduate-auditions.
Audition Dates & Information Spring Admission: Saturday, November 19, 2016 (flute applicants not accepted for spring admission) Fall Admission: Please review the Graduate audition website for dates specific to your instrument: https://music.asu.edu/admissions/graduate-auditions DMA applicants who are invited to audition after submitting prescreening materials must perform a live, on-campus audition. Recorded auditions are acceptable for master’s degree performance applicants only and must be uploaded online by November 1. CD/DVD audition recordings are not accepted. To be considered for a music scholarship or teaching assistantship, a live, on-campus audition is preferred. Ad hoc auditions may be scheduled with faculty (required for organ applicants), but must be completed by December 1 for Spring admission and February 28 for Fall admission. Flute applicants are not considered for admission to any spring semester. We welcome you to contact us via email to MusicAdmissions@asu.edu if you have any additional questions. We also encourage you to refer to the School of Music Web site, music.asu.edu, as a resource for your admissions questions. Best wishes, Office of Admissions School of Music Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts Arizona State University music.asu.edu | musicadmissions@asu.edu {!Case.Thread_Id}
